transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess I’m here because the clinic was getting on my case about how little I’ve been eating lately. But honestly, most days I’m just grabbing a coffee before my shift at the warehouse. It gets so incredibly loud in there, you know? The conveyor belts are constantly squeaking, and my supervisor, Dave, is always yelling over the noise to get the boxes taped up faster. It gives me such a headache by the end of the day. 

But yeah, maybe I'll have a yogurt or just a few bites of something after my GED class. The class is over at the community center, and I swear they haven't updated the building since the eighties. The chairs have those weird metal legs that scrape so loud on the linoleum every time someone shifts around. It's super distracting when you're trying to focus on math. 

But anyway, sitting down for a real, actual meal... I don't know, it just feels like it throws off everything I’m trying to keep in line.
How much weight have you lost recently, and do you feel like you're intentionally eating less than you used to?

I haven't been keeping track of the exact pounds, but yeah, I guess it's intentional. Like, my work pants are getting really loose on me lately. Which is actually kind of a pain because Dave is so strict about the dress code. He made this huge deal last week about a guy wearing the wrong shade of khaki, like, who even cares? It's a warehouse, we're just taping boxes. I had to go to that thrift store on 4th street just to find a belt that actually holds my pants up now. Have you been to that one? It always smells like mothballs and old soup, but they have decent stuff if you dig through the bins long enough. 

But um, anyway, what were we talking about? Oh, the weight. Yeah, people keep telling me I look too thin. But honestly, when I see the number on the scale go down, I feel like I’m finally getting somewhere, you know? Like I'm actually doing something right. So I really don’t see why I should be pushed to put it all back on just because they're bothered by it.
Do you consider yourself to be overweight or feel that you need to lose weight, even though others may say you’re too thin?

I mean, I know what other people say, but... yeah, I still feel like I need to lose more. Like, when I look in the mirror before my GED class, or before softball, my stomach and my thighs still just look way bigger than they should be. And honestly, how they look in the mirror basically decides my whole mood—it makes me feel like I’m either doing really good or just completely failing for the entire day. 

Which is really stressful, especially on softball days. I play in this slow-pitch league with some of the guys from the warehouse, and the jerseys they ordered for us this season are just hideous. They’re this blinding, neon orange color, like we're giant traffic cones or something. And the fabric is that cheap, scratchy polyester that doesn't breathe at all. When we play on Saturdays over at Centennial Park, you just start sweating the second you put it on. The dugout there doesn't even have a roof, so you're just baking in the sun while you wait to bat. Our umpire last week was sweating so much he had to keep stopping the game to take off his mask and wipe his glasses on his shirt... 

Um, but wait, what were you asking me? Oh, right, my weight. Yeah, I just... I don't see what they see. I still see a lot I need to fix.
Do you ever make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or exercise excessively to control your weight or shape?

No, I don't do any of that. Like, making myself sick or taking pills? Definitely not. And honestly, I don't really have the energy to work out a bunch besides my softball games. Plus, my job is basically a workout anyway. I'm on my feet all day at the warehouse, lugging these heavy boxes around. 

Actually, Dave—my supervisor—he's been on this huge power trip lately about who gets to use the motorized pallet jack. He locked the keys in his office because someone scratched the paint on the side of it last week. It's a piece of warehouse equipment! Who cares if the paint is scratched? So now we all have to use the manual ones, and the wheels on the one I usually grab are completely shot. It squeaks so loud, and it pulls to the left so hard you feel like you're wrestling a bear just to get a pallet of packing tape down the aisle. My shoulders are practically dead by the time my shift is over, so the last thing I want to do is go on a run or something... 

Wait, sorry, what did you ask me? Oh, right, throwing up and stuff. No, I just eat less. I don't do any of that other stuff.
Has your concern about your weight or shape caused any problems with your work, school, or relationships with others?

I mean, I'm still showing up to the warehouse every day, and I go to my GED classes, so it's not like I'm completely falling apart. But I guess... yeah, it does get in the way sometimes. Like, I've been saying no a lot when people from church want to go out to eat after service. Which is kind of a bummer because they usually go to this diner on Elm Street, and the waitresses there are so nice. They have these really cool retro uniforms, like the pink dresses with the white aprons? It feels like you stepped into a time machine. The owner, Sal, he's always sitting in the corner booth doing crossword puzzles. He actually gave me a free coffee once because I helped him figure out a six-letter word for "type of cloud." It was stratus, by the way. I only knew that because we watched this weird documentary in science class back in middle school where the narrator had the most monotone voice ever. I think half the class fell asleep... 

Wait, what was the question? Oh, problems with stuff. Yeah, so I skip the church lunches because I just need to keep my eating totally controlled, you know? And honestly, I've been leaving a lot of my GED homework unfinished lately because I'm just so focused on my schedule and what I'm eating. It just takes up a lot of space in my head.
Do you have an intense fear of gaining weight or becoming fat, even though you are currently underweight?

Yeah, I mean... it's terrifying, honestly. If I eat something like, I don't know, a piece of fried food someone brought into the break room, or if I were to actually eat a big plate of food at one of those church lunches, I get so scared it's going to show on me right away. Like, instantly. I'll just keep thinking about it non-stop, and all I want to do is go check the scale to make sure I didn't ruin everything. 

Which is why the break room at work is an absolute nightmare right now. Brenda from shipping just had her 50th birthday, and her daughter brought in this massive sheet cake from Costco. You know the ones? With the two inches of buttercream frosting that's basically just solid sugar and food coloring. It was bright blue, and it stained everyone's teeth. They left the leftovers sitting on the table next to the microwave, and it's been there for three days. Every time I go in there to get a water, it's just sitting there, staring at me. And the fridge in there smells terrible right now anyway because someone left their tuna salad in there over the long weekend. I told Dave he needs to clean it out, but he's too busy guarding his precious pallet jack keys...

Um... sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, right. Gaining weight. Yeah, I just... I'm really scared of it. Even if people say I'm small, I just can't risk it.
